For compatibility

I think [`atan2`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/780b6891e6f2a99e860a8c30eaf4c3dd6fdd13f7/core/math/transform_2d.cpp#L82-L84) followed by [`sin` and `cos`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a4bbad2ba8a8ecd4e756e49de5c83666f12a9bd5/core/math/vector2.cpp#L112-L118) is not the best approach here.

Try [`Transform2D::basis_xform`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a4bbad2ba8a8ecd4e756e49de5c83666f12a9bd5/core/math/transform_2d.h#L202-L206) followed by `Vector2::normalized` instead; that will just be a bunch of multiplications and additions and one square root.

(The same goes for all other occurrences of this pattern.)
It's wrong to call this for an area, so it should be an `ERR_FAIL_COND` similar to the one below.

Not such a big deal here but we have `Vector2::orthogonal()` that you can use instead.

The same goes for CollisionShape2D.
The `normalized()` is redundant because the setter does it already.
A default value of `Vector2(0, 1)` would make more sense here. This value also ends up in the documentation.

I was following this pattern:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104736/changes#diff-87820bbdf1f3f31603309d3295d4b198eaf1a99754d13dcbc924c7a41b506283R361

I also see this:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104736/changes#diff-87820bbdf1f3f31603309d3295d4b198eaf1a99754d13dcbc924c7a41b506283R573

I don't have an opinion on this, but it seems to be handled a bit inconsistently in this file. Can you confirm that you'd like it to be an error?
This is transforming by the wrong transform, it should be transforming by `col_obj_shape_xform` (as it was in `master`).

This will break (non-GDExtension) user scripts that use this method of `PhysicsServer2D`. The default should be `Vector2(0,1)` everywhere; the remaining ones are the one on this line and the one in `physics_server_2d_dummy.h` (though it doesn't really matter there).
